headerEntries.note: Cell contains only a short red dash/tick, not legible digits. Checksum (US 43 1/4 + this = KP 94 7/8) implies 51 5/8, identical to the DT-BS value directly above; likely an unwritten repeat marker rather than a fresh entry. Reported value is inferred, not directly read.

cells.note: A stray mark near this digit could suggest a fraction bleeding from the row below (43 3/4), but checksum US+BS=KP (45 + 52 1/2 = 97 1/2, matching KP entry exactly) confirms plain 45 with no fraction.

Numerator glyph is blurred at source resolution under high zoom; does not cleanly match the '3' shape used in the row above (June 29's 3/4), but no alternative digit is clearly legible either. Transcribed as '3/8' per both independent passes' consensus best-guess. Underline confirmed absent (plain grid line, not a hand-drawn mark) by close visual inspection.

Numerator glyph is a thin single stroke matching the '1' style used elsewhere (compared directly at 10x zoom against the nearby '5' in BS's 50 1/4, which has a distinct flat-top hook shape not present here). Read as 93 1/8 per the literal glyph. Checksum (US 43 3/8 + BS 50 1/4 = 93 5/8) does not reconcile with either the US or KP entries as written on this date; flagged as a probable inconsistency in the original ledger rather than force-fit to the checksum. [Corrected 93 1/8 -> 93 5/8 by KP checksum: 43 3/8 + 50 1/4 = 93 5/8; ambiguous fraction glyph at this resolution.]

annotations.text: On June 16th, the price of Bethlehem Steel was recorded in the Natural Reaction column. Refer to Explanatory Rule 6-B.
On June 28th, the price of U. S. Steel was recorded in the Natural Reaction column. Refer to Explanatory Rule 6-B.
On June 29th, the price of Bethlehem Steel was recorded in the Downward Trend column, being a price lower than the last price recorded in the Downward Trend column.
On July 13th, prices of U. S. Steel and Bethlehem Steel were recorded in the Secondary Rally column. Refer to Explanatory Rule 6-G.

notes: Chart Eleven spans dated rows June 2, 1939 through July 14, 1939 (only five rows carry handwritten entries: June16, June28, June29, June30, July13). Header (carried-forward pivotal) entries sit in four stacked rows above the "1939 / DATE" row, alternating DT(red)/NR(blue) pairs across the three instrument groups. Column assignment for the June 28-30 U.S. Steel figures was determined via the printed annotation (Natural Reaction column) rather than raw x-position alone, since adjacent narrow columns (DT vs NRC) are easy to conflate; the checksum rule (KP = US + BS) was used to resolve two ambiguous digits (US 45 on 6/28, and KP fraction on 6/30, read as 5/8 rather than the visually similar 1/8). One header cell (BS, third row, Downward Trend) contains only a short red dash with no legible digits; its reported value (51 5/8) is checksum-inferred, not directly read, and is flagged uncertain.
